assign.request: the visual hierarchy is so bad. Like, there's not enough padding on the preview cards... I like the flush cards... However, then the cards themselves need, if our default padding, if that's our default padding, which it should be, then the default padding system is broken.
steps: Measure every rail row's padding and which rule sets it
Write why.md: table plus the cause
Shared-page before/after shots and layout-check (if shared CSS changed)

log.msg: usage refresh skipped: ai/usage.json is outside this brief's fence

Measured at 1920 (rail 351px): every row is padded 8.8px 11.2px by ai2.css's own .ai2-row { padding: 0.55em 0.7em } (layer theme, nothing overrides it). The default word for a framed box, --pad-card, would give 16px here. Title line-height 28.8px (1.8, the theme's prose leading) so a 7-line title stands 201px. The three sub-lines use three different hand margins (0.15em, 0.3em, 0.35em). The time sits v-centred against a tall title.

decision.question: Is the cause the default padding system, or AI 2 not using it?
options: Make AI 2 use --pad-card and a rail-scale --gap
decision.why: --pad-card resolves to 16px in this rail and scales with the rail's width by design; the rows simply wrote 0.55em 0.7em instead, following the css skill's line that 'a control or row keeps its own em'. A preview card is a framed box, not a control. No shared CSS changes, so no shared-page shots are needed.

decision.question: How do gaps inside a 351px rail stop scaling with the window?
options: Declare .ai2-rows a size container so --gap reads the rail (framework.css's own stated design)
decision.why: framework.css says --gap's cqi 'reads the nearest container'; without one, a 351px rail got the 3440 window's 43px gap. One container makes every --gap rung inside the rail follow the rail.

assign.now: writing the fix in ai2.css and the row-head markup

findings.text: The requirements' deliverable 4 asks for a zero-console-error / zero-failed-request check on /framework/ai2/, a card, and the three shared pages, but neither `task.jsonl` nor `why.md` records that check having run — worth a quick pass before calling the task fully landed, even though the fix only touched `ai2.css`/`.js` (no shared CSS, per `why.md`'s own note).

`why.md`'s "before/after" measurement table (task.jsonl:62, why.md rows) looks right against the shots: `shots/before-ai2-1920.png` rows sit flush against each other with no visible inset, `shots/after-ai2-1920.png` and `shots/after-rail-zoom.png` show a clear 16px inset and consistent spacing between title/sub-line/bar, matching the stated cause (rows hand-padded 0.55em 0.7em instead of using `--pad-card`).

The fix stays inside the fence (`ai2/ai2.css`, `ai2/faces.js`, `ai2/live.js`, `ai2/page.js`, `ai2/real.js`, `ai2/doc/*`, task dir) and correctly avoids shared CSS since the cause was local (AI 2 never used `--pad-card`), matching the owner's own diagnosis was tested and found half-right: the default padding system itself was fine, AI 2 just wasn't using it.

`.ai2-row-head` and its children are only referenced inside `public/framework/ai2/` (plus two unrelated catalog/census JSON data files), so dropping `v-center` in favor of a scoped `align-items: flex-start` rule can't have broken another page.

AI 2 and the card: one 404 each, /framework/ai/usage.json, which is gitignored and so absent from every worktree; it was there before this change too. padding-check on /framework/ai2/: clean at 400, 1280, 1920, 3440.
